title: speculative-decoding-and-model-integration-draft
content:
Status: DRAFT / in_review
Owning authors: Michael Chen (owner), Priya Nandakumar (KV + cache), Lucas Romero (kernels + perf), Sara Ibrahim (rollout + metrics)
Last updated: 2025-02-20

Purpose / goals
- Draft a concrete design for adding speculative decoding support to the serving runtime and document how this interacts with kernel selection, scheduling, and the KV cache.
- Define model integration acceptance criteria (latency, correctness/regression constraints), rollback mechanics and related metrics to drive rollout decisions.
- Surface open questions and an initial testing/rollout plan for Dedicated/Hosted and Private deployments.

Background / motivation
- Speculative decoding (a.k.a. speculative execution / parallel-path decoding) reduces average latency by generating short candidate prefixes with a smaller/cheaper model (spec model) and validating them with the main model (oracle model). When successful it avoids repeated autoregressive token generation on the expensive model.
- We need a runtime-level design that composes with: kernel selection (precision/quantization), GPU scheduling/batching, and the KV cache so we preserve correctness while gaining latency/cost benefits.
- Also need clear integration acceptance criteria for onboarding a new model pair (spec -> oracle) into production, with rollback and metrics for safe rollouts.

Assumptions & terminology
- "Spec model": a small/fast model used to produce speculative token prefixes.
- "Oracle model": the canonical production model whose outputs are authoritative.
- "Speculative batch": group of requests that will use speculative prefixes; validation happens on the oracle model.
- KV cache semantics: per-request key-value cache storing past key/values for autoregressive decoding. Cache has versioned entries keyed by (model, model-version, request-id).

High-level design
1) API surface (runtime config)
- New per-route config block: speculative_config { enabled: bool, spec_model: string, failure_policy: enum{fallback, retry, none}, max_prefix_len: int, validation_batch_size: int, validation_timeout_ms: int }
- Default off. Teams can enable per-route; Dedicated customers may disable for regulatory reasons.
- We expose instrumentation hooks and traces for each speculative attempt.

2) Request flow (simplified)
- Incoming request arrives -> route config says speculative enabled -> scheduler enqueues to spec path and oracle path as a dependent task.
- Spec path: use cheaper model runtime kernels and quantization profile; produce prefix P_spec quickly (bounded by max_prefix_len).
- Oracle validation: enqueue a validation job on the oracle model which consumes KV cache for initial context and verifies P_spec using a fast prefix-checking shader (see below) or by executing the oracle forward pass for the prefix.
- If validated: commit speculative tokens to the response and update KV cache accordingly (atomic commit). If not: oracle continues traditional decoding starting from last validated token.
- Failure policy: fallback (drop speculative tokens and decode with oracle), retry (try speculative again with adjusted params), none (treat spec as suggestion but always re-decode).

3) Kernel & quantization considerations
- Spec models must be tagged with a kernel profile. The runtime will prefer the fast runtime path (FP16/INT8 kernels) for spec models. Document adaptor layer to ensure kernels for spec/oracle have consistent tokenization and special token handling.
- Oracle kernels may have different KV layout (e.g., fused KV cache formats). We need an adapter to convert speculative model’s KV outputs into oracle KV formats OR avoid writing spec outputs into the main KV until commit. Preferred: keep spec KV local to speculative worker and only materialize commits as KV deltas on success.

4) KV cache semantics and consistency
- Per-request KV namespaces: production KV cache entries are logically grouped by (request-id, model, model-version).
- Speculative execution writes into ephemeral KV (in-memory ephemeral store tied to the speculative job). On commit, we apply KV delta to the authoritative KV with a single atomic operation (update pointer + tokens).
- If the oracle's tokenizer/model vocabulary differs, we must not commit: requirement for model-pair validation that tokenization and special-token mapping are compatible. This is part of model integration acceptance checks.

5) Scheduling & batching interactions
- Spec path should have low latency scheduling priority but still be batchable. We expect many short spec runs — grouping them into micro-batches (N=8..32 based on observed load) yields efficiency.
- Oracle validation requires synchronous work after spec success/failure but is batched independently. The scheduler must support dependent jobs: spec job emits a validation task that can be coalesced across requests when they reach validation point.
- Backpressure rules: if validation queue is saturated we can (a) pause further speculative execution for that route, or (b) reduce max_prefix_len for new spec attempts. Configurable by route/customer.

6) Latency / correctness tradeoffs and heuristics
- Heuristics to decide when to run spec: route-level traffic patterns, historical spec success rate per prompt template, and per-customer policy.
- Conservative default: spec only prefixes up to 2 tokens; allow experiments for longer prefixes once success metrics stabilize.

Speculative validation implementation options
- Full-check: run oracle forward pass for full spec prefix and compare logits/next-token predictions. Pros: correct. Cons: expensive; duplicates compute.
- Prefix hash / quick-check: compute a small fingerprint or run a small forward that checks top-k membership. Pros: faster. Cons: possibility of false acceptances; must be bounded and measured.
- Proposed hybrid: do top-1/3 membership checks using a reduced compute path on oracle kernels (e.g., compute only final logits via a shallow reforward of last attention blocks) — requires kernel support and profiling.

Model integration: acceptance criteria and onboarding checklist
- Model pair metadata required: tokenization compatibility, model-version tag, kernel profile, expected max_prefix_len, suggested validation strategy, historical spec_success_rate (test harness), safety/filters compatibility.
- Integration tests (preflight):
  - Unit: tokenization equivalence tests across seed prompts.
  - Perf: end-to-end latency benchmarks with spec enabled vs disabled under controlled load.
  - Correctness/regression: automated prompt set (N ~ 2k) to measure exact-match and semantic drift thresholds.
  - Failure-mode tests: simulate oracle slowdowns / validation queue saturation and validate fallback behaviors.
- Acceptance thresholds (initial):
  - Spec success rate >= 45% on the regulated prompt set for 2-token prefixes, with p95 latency improvement >= 12% and p99 not worsened by >5ms.
  - No semantic regression (measured by eval harness) exceeding delta of 1.5% (task-dependent) on core prompt sets.
  - Memory overhead: ephemeral KV per request must be below X KB (we'll quantify after perf runs).

Rollback & safety mechanisms
- Immediate rollback: route-level toggle to disable speculative_config. Implemented as config push that stops scheduling spec tasks for new requests. Existing in-flight speculative tasks are allowed to finish (but can be canceled if needed).\- Canary rollback: if metric triggers during rollout, automatically disable for the impacted route/region and notify SRE/owners.
- Safe defaults for Private deployments: default OFF; must be enabled explicitly via admin API.

Metrics & instrumentation (things to record per-spec attempt)
- spec_attempt_count (counter)
- spec_success_count (counter)
- spec_success_rate = spec_success_count/spec_attempt_count
- spec_prefix_len_hist (histogram)
- added_latency_ms (how much spec adds when it fails)
- latency_saved_ms (how much spec saved when it succeeds)
- validation_queue_length (gauge)
- KV_commit_time_ms (histogram)
- spec_memory_overhead_bytes (histogram)
- rollout_trigger_events (counter with tags: route, region, customer)
- Model-pair specific: per-prompt-template success rate, false_acceptance_rate (cases where spec validated but semantic drift detected later)

Instrumentation notes
- Structured logs for each attempt with fields: request_id, route, spec_model, oracle_model, prefix_len, validation_strategy, success(bool), timings (spec_time, validation_time, kv_commit_time), memory_delta, failure_reason.
- Traces: attach speculative subspans to the main request trace. This allows end-to-end latency flamegraphs.

Testing & rollout plan
- Phase 0: internal perf/regression lab testing with synthetic load (1 team)
- Phase 1: limited canary to internal product routes (5% traffic), collect metrics for 48h, monitor p50/p95/p99 latency and spec_success_rate and false_acceptance_rate.
- Phase 2: gradual ramp 5->25->50% across regions, block if spec_success_rate drops below threshold or p99 latency regression exceeds 5ms.
- Phase 3: GA if stable across 7-day window.

Operational concerns & open questions
- How to best represent KV deltas and efficiently apply commits in the presence of different memory layouts across kernels? (Action: Priya to prototype KV delta object and atomic commit API)
- What validation strategy yields best ROI given kernel constraints? Need perf experiments (Lucas).
- Billing / attribution: how to reflect spec run cost savings in per-token billing metrics? (Product/Finance)
- Safety: verify compatibility with real-time safety filters; speculative tokens must flow through filters before commit. Potential double-filter cost.

Next steps / action items
- Priya: prototype ephemeral KV store + commit API (ETA 2 weeks).
- Lucas: microbench kernels: implement lightweight final-logit pass for oracle and measure perf (ETA 3 weeks).
- Michael: add runtime config hooks and proto route config parsing (ETA 1 week).
- Sara: draft monitoring dashboards and alert thresholds for canary (ETA 1 week).
- Team: schedule design review (target: 2025-02-27).

Notes to reviewers (informal)
- This is a working doc — expect rough edges and TODOs. Focus feedback on KV consistency model and validation strategy tradeoffs.
- If you know of prior art we should copy (e.g., Google or Microsoft papers on speculative decoding), paste links in the linked_artifacts list.
